title: Specialized Products Derived from Amino Acids
objectives: Identify key biomolecules synthesized from amino acids
Describe biosynthetic pathways and regulatory mechanisms
Understand clinical correlations of metabolic disorders
Explain the physiological roles of specialized products

overview.title: Product Categories
overview.content:
Specialized Derivatives

Key products derived from amino acids:

  • Neurotransmitters (Catecholamines, GABA, Serotonin)
  • Energy metabolites (Creatine, CoA, Carnitine)
  • Signaling molecules (NO, Histamine, Thyroid hormones)
  • Cofactors (THF, DHB, SAM, NAD+, FAD)

neurotransmitters.title: Neuroactive Compounds
neurotransmitters.content:
Neurotransmitters

1. Catecholamines

  • Precursor: Tyrosine
  • Pathway: Tyr → DOPA → Dopamine → Norepinephrine → Epinephrine
  • Key Enzymes:
    • Tyrosine hydroxylase (THB, O2)
    • DOPA decarboxylase (PLP)
    • Dopamine β-hydroxylase (Cu2+, ascorbate)
    • PNMT (SAM)
  • Disorders: Parkinson's (low dopamine), Pheochromocytoma (excess catecholamines)

2. Serotonin (5-HT)

  • Precursor: Tryptophan
  • Pathway: Trp → 5-HTP → Serotonin
  • Functions: Mood regulation, vasoconstriction
  • Carcinoid Syndrome: Tumor-induced overproduction (↑5-HIAA in urine)

3. GABA

  • Precursor: Glutamate
  • Synthesis: Glutamate decarboxylase (PLP)
  • Role: Major inhibitory neurotransmitter
  • Epilepsy: Associated with GABA deficiency

energy_metabolites.title: Energy Metabolism
energy_metabolites.content:
Energy-Related Compounds

1. Creatine/Phosphocreatine

  • Precursors: Glycine, arginine, methionine
  • Pathway: Guanidinoacetate → Creatine → Phosphocreatine
  • Function: Muscle energy buffer (ATP regeneration)
  • Clinical Marker: Creatinine clearance tests renal function

2. Coenzyme A

  • Components: Cysteine, pantothenate, ATP
  • Synthesis: 4-step pathway consuming 2 ATP
  • Role: Acyl group carrier in metabolism

signaling_molecules.title: Signaling Molecules
signaling_molecules.content:
Cell Signaling

1. Histamine

  • Precursor: Histidine (PLP-dependent decarboxylation)
  • Roles: Allergic response, gastric acid secretion
  • Derivatives: Carnosine (muscle/brain), ↓3-methylhistidine in Wilson's disease

2. Polyamines

  • Examples: Putrescine, spermidine, spermine
  • Functions: DNA packaging, cell proliferation
  • Effects: High doses cause hypothermia/hypotension

protective_molecules.title: Protective Compounds
protective_molecules.content:
Cellular Protection

Glutathione (GSH)

  • Structure: γ-Glu-Cys-Gly tripeptide
  • Functions:
    • Redox buffer (maintains -SH groups)
    • Detoxifies peroxides
    • RBC protection from oxidative damage

clinical.title: Clinical Correlations
clinical.content:
Clinical Applications

Diagnostic Markers

  • VMA/HVA: Catecholamine metabolites (pheochromocytoma)
  • 5-HIAA: Serotonin metabolite (carcinoid syndrome)
  • Creatinine: Muscle mass/renal function indicator

Therapeutic Targets

  • GABA analogs for epilepsy/hypertension
  • MAO/COMT inhibitors in Parkinson's
  • Antihistamines for allergies

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
FAQs

Q: Why does carcinoid syndrome cause flushing? +

A: Tumor-overproduced serotonin acts as a potent vasoconstrictor, followed by reactive vasodilation causing characteristic bluish-red facial flushing.

Q: How is creatinine used to assess kidney function? +

A: Creatinine is produced at a constant rate from muscle creatine and rapidly excreted by kidneys. Elevated blood levels indicate impaired glomerular filtration.

Q: Why are PLP-dependent enzymes clinically significant? +

A> Vitamin B6 (PLP precursor) is required for decarboxylases synthesizing dopamine, serotonin, GABA, and histamine - all crucial neurotransmitters.
